newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Pearl Oriental says no knowledge of probe.
newsitem.headline: Pearl Oriental says no knowledge of probe.

text.p: Luxury property developer and hotelier Pearl Oriental Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it knew of no probe into the company by Hong Kong securities regulators.
Pearl Oriental's share price suffered a dramatic fall in heavy trade on Thursday on rumours that the company was under investigation by securities regulators.

"We would like to confirm that the company has no knowledge of any investigation by the SFC (Securities and Futures Commission) nor had we ever received any query from the SFC in this respect," executive director Edwin Yu said in a statement made at the request of the stock exchange on Thursday.
The shares tumbled 35.84 percent, or HK$0.62, to close at HK$1.11 after touching a low of a year-low of HK$1.03 on trade of HK$708.13, making it the fourth most-actively traded issue.
The statement also addressed recent market rumours regarding the company's financial position and that of its chairman, who is its major shareholder.
"The company is financially strong and has adequate financial resources ready for any possible acquisition projects," it said.

The chairman told a new conference called to launch the company's latest hotel project on Wednesday that he had pledged just three percent of his shareholding in the company as collateral for a standby (bank) facility, not a substantial portion of the holding as reported in the local press.
"My total shareholding is 64.35 percent and I have only pledged 3.0 percent for this facility," said Wong. Pearl Oriental has total issued share capital of 9.38 billion shares.
Brokers said the company had a strong following of mainland Chinese investors, who may now be selling shares and repatriating funds to the mainland.

One regional brokerage analyst said investors did not like the company's latest hotel project. Pearl Oriental, which owns and manages several hotels in Hong Kong, Taiwan and China, plans to sell rooms in its latest project to individual investors.
"The deal is a novel one for Hong Kong at least," said the analyst. "But many investor may think that the company needs to raise cash."

The company will retain the management of the entire hotel, and investors will lease back their rooms in this four-star hotel to the hotel operating company and share in the total profit from the hotel services, said Wong.
